doc.title: Ken Peplowski interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 10, 1997 [interview 1 of 2]

chapter: Dorsey band and moving to New York
title: Artie Shaw band interview, Dick Johnson, and Annie tour
summary: Morrow tried to get him the Artie Shaw band leader job; Dick Johnson got it. Then eight months on the road with Annie.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Who did they get for that?

He lives in Boston. In fact the ironic thing is Dick used to play in Buddy Morrow’s band in the early 1950s. And Dick is a wonderful clarinet player and a very nice guy too. And he’s a man you might want to talk to, he’s an interesting guy. But he did a lot for me. So that was my big job experience. And then moving to New York after that, you know I was scared to death. I didn’t know anybody and I was there about six months before I even got any work. Oh in between that I did eight months on the road with “Annie,” just to make some money. And I have to tell you, this show, about the little kid and the orphans and the Christmas tree and the dog, this was the wildest time I’ve ever had in my entire life. Because the music was so boring and the mothers were traveling with the kids and it was unbelievable. I’ve never experienced anything like this in rock circles, in jazz circles, a constant party going on, everybody sleeping with everybody else, the mothers were having affairs with the musicians, I mean it was unbelievable. And so I did eight months and then I thought, I’d better get out of here because I’m going to wind up, you know.
Like this show is so squeaky clean, we’re going to go the other way.
Exactly. I could write a book, and maybe I will some day, about that time I had on that show.
